caption: A glass thermometer is lowered into a mug of hot water, and its red column climbs.

sa.check: The thermometer is lowered into a mug of hot water.
The column slows as it settles.
The bulb is in the water.
The lowering comes first and the climbing follows.

pc.expect: The column starts to rise once the bulb is in the water and not before.
pc.fail: The column rises before the bulb reaches the water; or the bulb sits in the hot water and the column stays where it was to the end of the clip; or the column rises while the thermometer is held in the air; or the column falls as the bulb enters the hot water.

pc.expect: The column only rises while the bulb stays in the hot water and then holds; it does not fall back while the water stays hot.
pc.fail: The column falls back while the bulb stays in the hot water; or the column rises and falls in turn; or the column jumps up and down between frames; or the column rises past the tube's top and out of it.

pc.expect: The column is a continuous thread of liquid in the tube that moves along it, and the glass stays rigid.
pc.fail: The column breaks into separate beads that move apart; or the column moves as a solid rod that sticks out of the tube; or the glass bends in the hot water; or the column spreads sideways to fill the tube unevenly.

pc.expect: The thermometer hangs or stands in the mug with its bulb down and the water lies level around it.
pc.fail: The thermometer floats out of the water and hangs above it; or the water climbs the thermometer's tube and stays; or the water's surface tilts and stays tilted with the mug level; or the thermometer rises bulb first out of the mug.

pc.expect: One thermometer in one mug; the glass stays whole and the column stays inside it.
pc.fail: The thermometer breaks and the liquid spills; or a second thermometer appears; or the column's liquid passes out through the glass; or the thermometer passes through the mug's wall.

pc.expect: Everything in view, named in the caption or not, keeps its number, identity and shape unless something visible acts on it, and nothing passes through anything else.
pc.fail: An object that nothing visible acts on appears from nothing; or vanishes while still in frame and not occluded; or duplicates or merges with another; or turns into a different object or a different shape between frames; or any object passes through another. Changes brought about by the caption's event or by a visible interaction, objects leaving the frame, and occlusion are not failures.

pc.expect: The thermometer's scale, the mug and the surroundings stay the same.
pc.fail: The scale's markings change; or the mug changes pattern; or items around the mug rearrange.

note: How far the column climbs is not judged, only that it rises after the bulb is wetted and does not fall back.
